subject: Dedicated capacity options for NexaHealth — cluster scaling playbook

From: Priya Gupta <priya.g@nexahealth.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity options — NexaHealth proof-of-value

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the demo earlier — the team is excited about Redwood's latency numbers. We're trying to map out what a short proof-of-value (PoV) would look like from a capacity perspective, and we need a couple of concrete options for our procurement and infra teams. High-level asks:

- A minimal configuration we can start with (cost-friendly, to validate throughput for our 50k monthly active API calls).
- A production-ready minimum commit that meets our 99th percentile latency SLO of 200ms for short chat queries (<=256 tokens).
- A phased ramp (4–12 weeks) with clear checkpoints and a suggested fallback plan if usage spikes.

Can you share a short options matrix (cluster size, minimum GPUs, expected concurrency, basic SLA impact, and rough monthly cost) we can attach to our internal eval? Procurement also asked for an initial BOM and an operations contact for escalation during the PoV.

Thanks — Priya

Priya — thanks for the clear asks. I'm looping in Marcus (AE) and Lauren (SE) to put together a concise options matrix and an ops escalation contact. Quick note on assumptions so our numbers align:

- "Short chat queries" means median prompt+response token length ~120 tokens, 99th percentile <=256 tokens.
- Expected steady-state concurrency target for PoV: please confirm if 25 qps peak or if you anticipate burstier patterns.

We can put three options in a single page: Starter (cost-min, low buffer), Baseline (recommended for PoV with monitoring & autoscale headroom), and Production-min (for SLA-backed usage). I'll attach a draft by end of day Friday.

Aisha Ramhan

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options — NexaHealth proof-of-value

Priya / team — attached is the initial options matrix (see attached spreadsheet row summary also pasted below). I kept the choices focused on latency-sensitive chat workloads and the ability to measure throughput vs cost during the PoV.

Summary (short):
- Starter: 4x A100-40GB equivalence (min GPUs = 4). Expected safe concurrency ~10–12 qps, burst to 18 qps with degraded 99p latency (~300–400ms). Lowest monthly burn; no SLA. Good for a proof of concept if Nexa wants minimal spend.

- Baseline (recommended for PoV): 8x A100-80GB equivalence (min GPUs = 8). Expected concurrency ~20–24 qps, burst to 35 qps with autoscale policies. 99p latency target ~180–220ms when batching and KV cache active. Includes monitoring, tracing hooks, and one weekly health call.

- Production-min (SLA-ready): 16x A100-80GB equivalence (min GPUs = 12 reserved, up to 16 burst). Designed to meet 99p <=200ms under a 25–30 qps sustained workload; includes SLA terms, accelerated support (24/7 on-call), and per-route cost controls.

Ramp schedule (recommended):
- Week 0: Provision Baseline cluster (8 GPUs) and run smoke tests with synthetic traffic.
- Weeks 1–2: Run PoV with real traffic (route-tagging + eval prompts); collect latency/cost metrics.
- Week 3: If metrics meet success criteria (99p latency <=220ms and steady throughput >=18 qps), increase to Production-min reserved level (12 GPUs reserved) with burst to 16.
- Week 4–8: Monitor & iterate; authorize final commitment if utilization >65% for two consecutive weeks.

Fallback plan: If latency regresses during PoV, we will enable: 1) temporary burst capacity to Production-min (subject to availability), 2) prefix KV caching for hot prompts, 3) roll back to larger instance types (fewer GPUs but more memory/parallelism) if model memory becomes bottleneck.

Attachments referenced: Nexa-MAP-ops.xlsx (options matrix), NX-dedicated-proposal-v2.pdf (one-pager).

—Lauren

lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options — NexaHealth proof-of-value

Thanks Lauren — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs from our infra team:

1) For the Baseline 8-GPU option, can you call out expected token-cost per 100k tokens and a rough monthly cost band (including reserved vs burst pricing)? Procurement needs a ballpark for initial budgeting (we'll refine after PoV).
2) With the ramp schedule, does Redwood guarantee availability of burst capacity to 16 GPUs within the 4-week window, or is that subject to fleet availability? We need to know if we should gate internal launch planning on that.

Also, procurement asked for a named operations escalation contact (phone + pager) for the PoV so they can list it in the runbook.

Best — Priya

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options — NexaHealth proof-of-value

Priya — quick answers and next steps:

1) Cost ballpark (Baseline 8-GPU): token-price ~ $0.0009 per token processed (model-dependent), estimate for 100k tokens -> $90; typical PoV month for expected traffic (50k MAU, ~15 qps peak) ~ $28k–$35k (includes reserved baseline + small burst buffer and monitoring add-ons). Detailed pricing table is in NX-dedicated-proposal-v2.pdf (attached).

2) Burst availability: Redwood offers a soft guarantee for burst-to-16 during the PoV window depending on regional capacity. For firm commitments we recommend reserving 12 GPUs (Production-min) and enabling a pre-approved burst credit — Marcus will work the commitment terms with procurement to lock availability if Nexa wants hard guarantees.

3) Ops contact: Dylan Brooks — On-call escalation. Phone: +1-415-555-0219; Pager: +1-415-555-1999; email: dylan_brooks@redwood.com. We'll provide a short runbook snippet (incident play, paging matrix) by Monday.

Next steps:
- Marcus to share procurement-friendly redlines and a simple SOW for the PoV (timeline + billing cadence).
- Lauren to deliver a short runbook and the one-page operations checklist.
- Aisha & Marcus to finalize the MAP+pricing doc and send to Nexa procurement by EOD Monday.

If that works, can we lock a 30-min alignment call next Wednesday 09/23 to sign off on the PoV success criteria?

Thanks — Aisha
